extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, philosophers of mathematics, and educated general readers interested in foundations of mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Survey of evaluative standards for mathematical concepts (esp. the infinite and real numbers), contrasting formalist, intuitionist, and pragmatic/philosophical criteria and showing their implications. Useful for assessing what makes a mathematical notion acceptable or 'real'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalist requirement: axiomatization and logical consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: We must devise a body of axioms which could serve as the basis of the theory and, to make sure that we are not again led astray by our intuition, we must construct a purely formal, logically consistent schematic outline of such a body, a mere skeleton without content. Having erected such a comprehensive, consistent system, we shall base the arithmetic of the infinite upon it as a foundation, secure in our conviction that no paradox or antinomy will ever arise again to disturb our peace of mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associated with Hilbert, Russell, and Zermelo; guidance is to build a formal axiomatic system and check for internal logical consistency. Example/appeal: Hilbert's dictum 'From the paradise created for us by Cantor, no one will drive us out.' Scoring note: emphasis is on formal completeness/consistency rather than empirical applicability; anti-pattern is relying on unrestricted intuitive use of 'all' or 'aggregate' without axiomatic control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intuitionist/constructibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In order that a concept may gain admission into the realm of mathematics, it is not enough that it be 'well defined': it must be constructible. Not merely must the concept exist in name, but also an actual construction should be given to determine the object which the concept represents. As to construction, the only admissible ones are the finite processes, or... such infinite processes as are reducible to finite by means of a finite number of rules. The act of conceiving simultaneously an infinite number of single objects and of treating the whole as an individual object does not belong to this category of admissible concepts and must a priori be barred from arithmetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associated with Kronecker, Brouwer, Weyl, and Poincaré. Practical guidance: accept only finite constructive procedures (or infinite ones with finite-rule reductions); reject treating actual completed infinities as legitimate mathematical objects. Implication: concepts like classical irrationals or unrestricted set-theoretic aggregates require profound modification or rejection. Anti-pattern: permitting non-constructive existence proofs or 'simultaneous' infinitary constructions without explicit construction rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrinsic standards for mathematical achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical achievement shall be measured by standards which are peculiar to mathematics. These standards are independent of the crude reality of our senses. They are: freedom from logical contradictions, the generality of the laws governing the created form, the kinship which exists between this new form and those that have preceded it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides evaluation of mathematical work from a mathematician's standpoint rather than empirical applicability. Examples: conic sections, imaginary numbers, differential calculus, matrices — initially abstract inventions that later proved applicable. Scoring note: prioritize internal coherence, generality/unifying power, and continuity with mathematical tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pragmatic/historical validity criterion: preserve and further the life of the race
rubrics_metrics.description: The issue is: to what extent has the conception preserved and furthered the life of the race? The falsest conceptions... are also those which are the most indispensable. The criterion of validity for any illusion is a post factum ... Those that preserve and further the life of the race thrive and grow, and thus earn their right to reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pragmatic, historical test: a mathematical concept's validity is judged retrospectively by its fruitfulness and usefulness in organizing experience and advancing knowledge. Examples cited: ideas once seen as 'mystical' (imaginary numbers, calculus, matrices) later vindicated by application. Scoring note: this is a posteriori; anti-pattern is rejecting ideas solely because they initially seem false or empirically unsupported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical compatibility test (physics and divisibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: When we turn to the question, what is the essence of the infinite, we must first account to ourselves for the meaning the infinite has for reality: ... nowhere in reality does there exist a homogeneous continuum in which unlimited divisibility is possible ... Planck discovered the energy-quanta. ... Einstein ... demonstrated the possibility of a finite world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance from Hilbert's account of physics: the physical sciences repeatedly find limits to divisibility (atoms, electrons, quanta) and cosmology allows finite models; hence unlimited divisibility/infinite continua are not empirically supported. Implication: do not treat the infinite as empirically necessary; use caution when appealing to empirical reality to justify mathematical infinitary concepts. Scoring note: weighs empirical evidence against treating mathematical infinities as real features of the physical world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical necessity and intuition as a separate acceptance criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The infinite is not an experiential nor a logical necessity; it is a mathematical necessity. This affirmation ... may be pure fiction, but it is a convenient and therefore a necessary fiction. It frees us from the burden of examining in each particular case whether what we assert about the case is at all possible. It lends to our statement that appearance of generality without which there would be no science; and above all it bridges the chasm between the inescapable conception of a world which flows in the stream of time, and the number concept which was born in counting the discrete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats certain idealizations (infinite processes, simplicity, uniformity, regularity, causality) as methodological necessities driven by mathematical intuition. Practical guidance: accept some fictions for their heuristic/unifying power while remaining aware they are not empirically or purely logically mandated. Scoring note: values convenience, generality, and the ability to systematize experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective reality as 'what is common to many' (Poincaré) and the circularity caution
rubrics_metrics.description: 'What we call objective reality is, in the last analysis, what is common to many thinking beings and could be common to all.' But efforts to judge the reality of numbers by the objective world run into a vicious circle because measuring instruments and scientific practice already presuppose arithmetic (e.g., the real number apparatus underlies rulers, thermometers, voltmeters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: if one attempts to use the objective—shared—world to validate number, be explicit about potential circularity: instruments and measurements assume number. Scoring note: avoid using empirical measurement as an independent test for number without addressing this dependency; anti-pattern is treating measurements as independent evidence that presuppose the very mathematical framework under assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social/language precondition for number's reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Counting presupposes a language, an institution which transcends the subjective reality or the immediate perceptions of any individual. An individual without a milieu, deprived of language... could not construct a science of number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for the possibility/acceptance of number: requires collective linguistic/institutional structures. Use this as analytic tool to assess whether a purported mathematical notion is meaningful in the absence of social-linguistic grounding. Implication: purely subjective sensory criteria cannot account for arithmetic; anti-pattern is ignoring the communal, linguistic roots of number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject reliance solely on subjective sensory reality when validating mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: If reality be restricted to the immediate experience of our senses, no thinking man... will attribute a reality to the concept [infinite]. If the subjective reality be taken as criterion of what is valid in mathematics, we shall be compelled not only to condemn the infinite process and all it implies, but to scrap the counting procedure as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: do not accept 'immediate sense impressions' as the sole arbiter for mathematical validity; such restriction would undermine counting and higher mathematics. Scoring note: emphasizes necessity of broader (objective/shared or formal/mathematical) standards rather than pure sensory evidence.
